items.title: What does it mean to 'know' your fans?
items.summary: At SBJ's Fan Data Roundtable, AMB Sports and Entertainment COO Tameka Rish defined knowing a fan as having consent and a way to communicate with them, and estimated her organisation knows about 30% of its attendees on average. The biggest gap is groups where one person scans everyone in, which also skews demographic data, especially for women. The PWHL's Jayne Bussman-Wise said 40% to 80% of its attendees are first-time visitors to the arenas it plays in, and the Red Sox's Jon Hay said frictionless, genuine incentives to engage digitally during games are the clearest path to fans identifying themselves.
items.what_it_means: Most sports organisations can identify only a minority of the people in their venues, and the gap is widest among the people who come with the ticket buyer.

items.title: Leagues increasingly helping teams know, reach their fans
items.summary: The NBA launched a leaguewide data initiative four years ago that pools fan data and shares it with teams, and this season it is making sure every team has a customer data platform, providing one at its own cost if necessary. The NHL gives teams a consolidated fan view that includes league events and merchandise data, and MLB clubs such as the Red Sox now have mostly real-time access to digital data that MLB once owned outright. The PWHL, a single-entity league, runs marketing, email, analytics and ticket operations centrally.
items.what_it_means: Leagues are becoming the data infrastructure for their clubs, which shifts the advantage to whichever clubs do the most with the shared data.

items.title: Answering the ticket sales conundrum
items.summary: At SBJ's Fan Data Roundtable, the NBA's Mike James said it is easy to keep selling tickets to businesses and people with money to spend, and asked what the industry has done to nurture first and second-time buyers if the market cools. The Detroit Lions' Ashton Mullinix said the club has sold out, has a waitlist of 20,000 people and has raised prices by more than 20% a year three times in a row. Aramark's Scott McDade cited research with Vision Insights finding 80% of premium buyers want a mix of experiences, and the PWHL's Jayne Bussman-Wise said fans want different kinds of nights at different times.
items.what_it_means: A sold-out market can hide a weak pipeline of new fans, which only shows when demand turns.

items.title: NFL teams build on their investments in Mexico ahead of league's return
items.summary: Ahead of the 49ers-Vikings game in Mexico City on 22 November, NFL teams with Mexico marketing rights describe the year-round work behind it. The 49ers say their fan base there has grown by more than 1,000% since 2022 on NFL measures, have been the top-selling team on NFL Shop in Mexico for five years and plan a flag football program in 75 schools. The Rams lean on Spanish-language social, youth flag football and a children's book, while the Chiefs used Spanish-first content to climb into the top five most popular NFL teams in Mexico.
items.what_it_means: International fan bases are built through year-round local presence, with the game itself as the showcase.

items.title: Nike ends Adidas' Champions League ball reign with €40m-a-year deal
items.summary: Nike will become the official match ball supplier of the UEFA Champions League from next season until the end of 2030/31, ending Adidas' 25-year association with the competition. Nike will also supply the Europa League and Conference League, the first time one company has covered all three UEFA men's club competitions. SportsPro understands the deal is worth around €40 million a year, which the Financial Times reported is double the current agreement, and it followed a competitive tender run by UC3 and Relevent Football Partners.
items.what_it_means: Category rights in elite football are repricing fast, and long incumbency counts for little when a rival will pay double.

items.title: NWSL Championship Shattering Ticket Records: 'Perfect Storm'
items.summary: On Monday morning the cheapest resale ticket for Saturday's NWSL Championship between the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current at Audi Field was $430, according to TicketData, when no previous NWSL final had passed $100. TicketData founder Keith Pagello put it down to the Spirit playing at home, brokers largely overlooking the event and heavy fan interest during the presale. Last season's final had a $64 get-in price, and prices peaked at $755 after the Spirit's semifinal win before easing.
items.what_it_means: Demand for women's sport is running ahead of how the market, resale brokers included, has been valuing it.

items.title: Sid Lee Sport partners with Guinness to measure the true commercial value of sports sponsorship
items.summary: Sid Lee Sport and sister agency Kepler are evaluating Guinness's global sports sponsorship portfolio across six markets, including Great Britain, Ireland and the United States, and nine rights holders including the Premier League, Arsenal and the Six Nations. The work analyses three years of sales, brand and partnership data to isolate the incremental commercial impact of the partnerships, looking past media exposure to pouring rights, fan research and activation. Sid Lee Sport's Mike Grumbridge said traditional exposure and reach metrics don't tell brands what their investment delivers commercially.
items.what_it_means: Major sponsors are moving the test of a partnership from exposure to incremental sales.

items.title: FanSided launches redesigned app with emphasis on personalized feeds, in-depth coverage
items.summary: FanSided's redesigned app, launched on 16 November by Minute, combines personalised team feeds, analysis, video highlights and, for the first time, live scores and game tracking. The aim is to convert part of an audience of more than 50 million monthly readers into regular app users and reduce reliance on search and social referrals. Founder Zach Best said success is about retention and frequency, and that the app competes on depth of team coverage rather than trying to out-score the national apps.
items.what_it_means: Sports publishers are moving to own direct audience relationships as search and social referrals become less dependable.

items.title: TikTok says more than 46,000 UK music creators have gone LIVE in 2026, with daily views up 74% YoY
items.summary: TikTok says more than 46,000 UK music creators went LIVE on the platform between January and mid-October 2026, and that UK music creators averaged 4.9 million global views a day on TikTok LIVE in September, up 74% year on year. The company positions the feature as a way for musicians to reach listeners worldwide without the cost and logistics of touring, with income from virtual gifts on top of gigs and recorded music. It released the figures alongside a TikTok LIVE music showcase in London featuring ArrDee and Matilda Mann.
items.what_it_means: Live music audiences are increasingly being built and monetised online between tours.

items.title: Bill Simmons ends ChatGPT deal after fan backlash
items.summary: SBJ reports that Bill Simmons has ended a ChatGPT sponsorship deal after fan backlash. The sponsored segments ran mainly on The Bill Simmons Podcast and The Ringer Fantasy Football Show and worked AI-generated prompts into the discussions. SBJ cites The Wrap's view that the move shows the limits of AI companies' push into podcast advertising, where paid integrations risk alienating the audiences they are meant to reach.
items.what_it_means: Sponsor integrations built into the content itself only work if the audience accepts the fit.
